target: Não fica triste, vai melhorar.
english: Don't be sad, it'll get better.
tip: Ficar here means to become, marking a change of state: ficar triste is get sad.

target: Fale com o gerente sobre isso.
english: Talk to the manager about that.
tip: To talk to someone, Portuguese uses falar com, not falar a: fale com o gerente.

target: Não se preocupe, tudo vai dar certo.
english: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
tip: Dar certo is a set phrase meaning to work out or turn out fine.

target: Pensa bem antes de tomar uma decisão.
english: Think carefully before making a decision.
tip: Decisions go with tomar, not fazer: tomar uma decisão means to make a decision.

target: Apaga a luz quando sair.
english: Turn off the light when you leave.
tip: After quando about a future event, use the future subjunctive: quando sair is when you leave.

target: Preencha o formulário com seus dados.
english: Fill out the form with your information.
tip: Preencher is to fill out a form; encher is to fill up with liquid: preencha o formulário.

target: Cadastre-se no site para receber as promoções.
english: Register on the site to receive promotions.
tip: In affirmative commands the pronoun attaches to the verb with a hyphen: cadastre-se.

target: Eu faria qualquer coisa pela minha família.
english: I would do anything for my family.
tip: Pela is por plus a, marking for the sake of: pela minha família.

target: Amanhã será um dia melhor.
english: Tomorrow will be a better day.
tip: Melhor is the irregular comparative of bom, so 'better' is melhor, never mais bom: será um dia melhor.

target: Nós vamos reformar a cozinha.
english: We're going to renovate the kitchen.
tip: Vamos plus an infinitive is the everyday future in Brazil, easier than the simple future: nós vamos reformar.

target: Quem chegar primeiro guarda lugar.
english: Whoever arrives first reserves a seat.
tip: Quem chegar uses the future subjunctive; for regular verbs it looks just like the infinitive, chegar.

target: Ele disse que viria mais cedo.
english: He said he would come earlier.
tip: In reported speech, the conditional viria expresses a future seen from the past: ele disse que viria.

target: Eu escolheria o prato de peixe.
english: I would choose the fish dish.
tip: The conditional ending -ia is the same for -ar, -er and -ir verbs, so escolher becomes escolheria.

target: Eu vou tentar resolver isso hoje.
english: I'll try to solve this today.
tip: Tentar is followed directly by the infinitive, with no preposition: vou tentar resolver isso.

target: A gente vai jantar fora hoje.
english: We're going to eat out tonight.
tip: A gente means 'we' but takes a singular verb, so it is a gente vai, never a gente vamos.

target: Vocês se importariam de esperar um pouco?
english: Would you mind waiting a bit?
tip: Importar-se de means 'to mind'; keep both the reflexive se and de: vocês se importariam de esperar.

target: Tudo o que eu quero é descansar.
english: All I want is to rest.
tip: Tudo o que means 'everything that'; the little o links tudo to the relative que: tudo o que eu quero.

target: Ela vai cortar o cabelo amanhã.
english: She's going to get a haircut tomorrow.
tip: Cortar o cabelo means 'get a haircut', even when the barber does it; Portuguese keeps the active verb.

target: Eu pagarei quando receber o salário.
english: I'll pay when I get my salary.
tip: pagarei is the simple future, which sounds formal or written in Brazil; speech would say vou pagar.

target: Eu vou te buscar no aeroporto.
english: I'll pick you up at the airport.
tip: Buscar means 'pick someone up', not just 'search': vou te buscar no aeroporto.

target: Você teria coragem de pular de paraquedas?
english: Would you have the courage to skydive?
tip: Ter coragem de plus an infinitive means 'to dare to': teria coragem de pular.

target: Eu vou parar de fumar este ano.
english: I'm going to quit smoking this year.
tip: Parar de plus an infinitive means 'to stop doing something': parar de fumar.

target: Ela vai estudar medicina no ano que vem.
english: She's going to study medicine next year.
tip: O ano que vem is the everyday way to say 'next year', literally 'the year that comes'.

target: O livro que eu comprei é muito bom.
english: The book I bought is very good.
tip: English can drop the relative ('the book I bought'), but Portuguese keeps que: o livro que eu comprei.

target: A casa cujo telhado vazou precisa de reforma.
english: The house whose roof leaked needs renovation.
tip: Cujo means 'whose' and agrees with the thing owned, not the owner: a casa cujo telhado vazou.

target: Será um prazer recebê-lo.
english: It will be a pleasure to welcome you.
tip: When o attaches to an infinitive ending in r, the r drops and a circumflex is added: receber plus o becomes recebê-lo.

target: Será que vai chover hoje?
english: Do you think it's going to rain today?
tip: Será que opens a question meaning 'I wonder' or 'do you think': será que vai chover hoje?

target: Eu moraria no Rio se pudesse.
english: I would live in Rio if I could.
tip: For hypotheticals, pair the conditional with se plus the imperfect subjunctive: eu moraria no Rio se pudesse.

target: A loja vai fazer uma promoção.
english: The store is going to have a sale.
tip: Promoção means a store sale or special offer, not a job promotion: a loja vai fazer uma promoção.

target: Eu ficaria muito feliz se você aceitasse.
english: I would be very happy if you accepted.
tip: Use ficar, not ser, for becoming happy or sad: eu ficaria muito feliz.
